For at the very least, they will be forced to look at the same moment to the principles, centers, periods, and figures of both motions. But if the Sun rests and the Earth moves, the motion of each planet is unique, and can be effected by physical magnetic virtues; with the animate faculty being required for scarcely more than a single rotation of the body of the Sun, [and] of the mind...

   **Twelfth**, from the source of motion. For it has just been demonstrated, and will be confirmed by more evidence below, that all motion of the five primary planets, and partly even the secondary ones, originates from the Sun. It is only right to believe that the first cause of motion is itself immobile. Therefore, the Sun remains immobile in its place; and consequently, the Earth is moved in an annual motion in place of the Sun.
   **Thirteenth**, from the instruments of motion. For if we allow the Sun and the Earth to rotate around their own axes, then the physical forms of these bodies become the subjects of the moving powers by which the six planets are moved by the Sun, and the Moon is moved by the Earth. But if the Sun travels in an annual motion while the Earth remains at rest, then there is no physical form of a body available to move the Sun or to provide the motion; nor does the Earth, if it is not rotated around its own axis in a daily period, have any means by which to move the Moon. But this argument presses more urgently on the daily motion.
   **Fourteenth**, regarding the motion of longitude, is as follows. If the Sun moves, carrying around the entire system of orbits, something new happens regarding it: for some body would be moving itself, or certainly be moved by a unique external mover, whereas the other primary bodies are moved by one common Sun, and thus by something other than themselves. But if the Earth moves in a circle, it is moved by the Sun just like the other primary planets, and nothing new occurs. Therefore, it is probable that the Earth moves, since a probable cause of its motion is apparent; while the Sun stands fixed.
   **Fifteenth**, the argument from the motion of altitude. it is argued that the Moon is balanced on a diameter extended toward the Sun; but if the Sun is established as moving, then on the contrary, the Earth becomes the cause of the Sun's slowness and speed, and thus also of its circuit. Yet let the bodies themselves of the Sun and Earth be inspected, and let a judgment be made: which is more probable? That the Sun—the source of motion for the five planets and many times larger than the Earth—should be moved by the Earth along with that Node <note>The intersection of orbital planes</note> of the five planetary systems? The sixteenth probability is this: that since in the first book the daily rotation of the Earth around its own axis was asserted by many arguments and solutions to objections—among which the strongest were that, by assuming the Earth's daily motion, both the final and instrumental cause of the obliquity of the Ecliptic <note>The 23.5-degree tilt of Earth's axis relative to its orbit</note> can be derived from the Earth itself. Neither of these can be explained if the Earth is at rest, nor can they be sought from the sphere of the fixed stars where the Zodiac resides, without respect to this tiny little body called Earth. Therefore, the translation <note>The movement from one place to another</note> of the Earth's center can no longer be considered so absurd. Indeed, probability suffices if the remaining arguments require the thing itself. For this should not be sold as a necessary argument: because even the Sun is rotated around its own axis, yet it remains immobile in its place as a whole.

The seventeenth reason: if the Earth travels in an annual motion, we find a more probable cause not only for the shifting of the Ecliptic itself from some fixed stars to others, than if we were to attribute this variation to the Sun (the primary body); but by the same labor, we provide the reason for the unequal progression of the planetary Nodes. Furthermore, by adopting the axis of the Earth's daily motion, we explain the causes of the changed obliquity of the Ecliptic, as well as a certain inequality in the precession of the equinoxes (though we rejected the entirety of that specific phenomenon in the third argument). Truly, the causes of so many phenomena must remain entirely unknown if the Earth does not travel in an annual motion.

The eighteenth argument is derived from the purpose of motion, by which it is proven that motion belongs to the Earth, as it is the dwelling place of a creature designed for contemplation. For it was not fitting that man, intended to be an inhabitant and observer of this world, should remain fixed in one single spot, as if in a closed chamber. In such a state, he would never have achieved the measurement and contemplation of stars so remote, unless he had been endowed with other gifts beyond the human. Rather, equipped with the eyes he now possesses and these faculties of the mind, he ought to walk about within this most spacious edifice by the annual transport of the Earth—his own home. He must take up different positions, as surveyors are accustomed to do; that is, he ought to travel so that he might more correctly gaze upon and measure the individual members of the house. You understand, of course, that so the first part of this fourth book could be composed, its author required the "ship" of the Earth and its annual voyage around the Sun. again concerning Jupiter, as it carries four satellites, and concerning Saturn, which carries two <note>At the time of Kepler's writing, only two of Saturn's moons—Titan and Rhea—were suspected or confirmed; we now know it has dozens.</note>: just as the Earth carries one, called the Moon: of which more will be said below.

***By what principles is this rotation of bodies around their own axes accomplished?***

It was stated in the first book concerning the Earth, and in this fourth book concerning the Sun, that these bodies are turned by an inherent animate principle or something similar <note>Kepler often used the term "anima" or "soul" to describe the internal force that drives a planet's rotation, a precursor to the concept of inertia and rotational energy</note>. However, it is gathered from two pieces of evidence that this principle is not acting alone in rotating the Earth, but is assisted by the Sun. First, because the number of the Earth's daily revolutions in a year, which is 365 and a quarter, exceeds the neighboring archetypal number of 360 <note>Kepler believed the universe was designed according to perfect geometric and harmonic "archetypes," where 360 represents a perfect circle</note>. For it is consistent that, unless the internal moving force of the Earth were invigorated by the perpetual presence of the Sun, the Earth would have moved somewhat more slowly around its axis: so that in the same annual space of time it would have made fewer revolutions, for instance, only 360. This being granted, it follows that the remaining and, as it were, "extra" five and a quarter revolutions are added to those 360 because of the assistance from the Sun.

*But if this had been the goal, it seems it would have been achieved; yet now you yourself admit that these ratios have been disturbed, since by those additional impulses from the Sun, instead of 360, there are now 365 days etc., and thus the daily journeys are shorter?*

->**How the Sun strengthens the motive power of the Earth, increasing the speed of the Earth's daily revolution?**<-

It is very probable that this happens by means of the Sun's light, which is poured into the Earth through the illumination of its hemisphere. For because the physical equation of time <term>Equation of Time: the difference between time kept by a clock and time kept by the sun's position</term> requires unequal daily revolutions of the Earth, according as its distances from the Sun vary; certainly at a short distance the illumination is strong, being from a denser light, and at a long distance it is weak, being from a thinner and thus lesser light; and this (as far as one dimension of length, in which the motion tends) is in the exact proportion of the distances. Thus the abundance of light, which exists at any given time, becomes fit—in place of the distances—to distribute this acceleration throughout the year.

*What are the effects of the Earth's daily revolution,*
*and in general, those of the primary bodies around*
*their own axes?*

Two: The first is specific to the Earth, namely that to us, the inhabitants of the Earth, all the stars of heaven—fixed and wandering <note>The "wandering stars" refer to the planets, from the Greek *planētēs*.</note>, and thus even the Sun and Moon—seem to rise daily from the east and set in the west; although, in respect to this daily motion, they actually remain fixed in their places. This deceptive appearance was dealt with in the first three books on spherical doctrine. The other effect is physical and most true, common to all primary bodies and even to the Sun itself: it is that the primary bodies, through the species <note>original: "speciem"; here Kepler refers to a physical force or "emanation" radiating from a rotating body.</note> emitted from their bodies while in a state of revolution, stir their secondary bodies—as the Earth stirs the Moon—and cause the secondary bodies to follow in the same direction, though more slowly, as if left behind.

*By what arguments is it made probable that*
*the primary bodies themselves provide the secondary bodies*
*with their motions around them, and especially the*
*Earth to the Moon?*

The Moon and Earth provide the first proof. For just as we reasoned above—from the fact that planets moving closer to the Sun are carried along more swiftly—that the Sun, through the species of its body (that is, being in a state of rotation), stirs the planets around itself in the same direction: so also, because we perceive that the Moon, 1. the closer it approaches the Earth (and not the Sun), the more rapidly it moves around the Earth; 2. and indeed in the same direction in which the Earth revolves around its axis; we derive that motion of the Moon from this rotation of the Earth with the highest probability. $\quad$ Since, therefore, there is such an exact agreement of the Jovian satellites with the six primary planets themselves: not only did we rightly conjecture above that Jupiter's body also turns around its own axis after the example of the Sun, so that the analogy might stand in all its members; but here we now furthermore confirm, not without reason, that this rotation of the primary bodies around their own axes is the cause of the circuit of the secondary bodies around their primaries. This is the 5th point, and all the more probable because we see that, just as the Sun is larger than all the planets which it moves, so also the Earth is much larger than its Moon, and Jupiter much larger than its satellites; and for that reason, they are as fit for moving others as the Sun is. The remaining similarities pertain again to the Moon. For 6th, the telescope has taught us that the bodies of the Moon and the Earth are kindred, as it provides evidence on the Moon of mountains and seas, such as exist on our globe of Earth. This kinship was even recognized by Aristotle—otherwise a most fierce defender of the "fifth essence" <term>Quintessence: the ancient belief that the heavens were made of a pure, unchanging element different from the four earthly elements</term> of the heavens—who, as Averroes reports, said the Moon seemed to be a certain "ethereal Earth." I shall remain silent regarding Plutarch and the other philosophers mentioned in Macrobius.

$\quad$ Just as, therefore, the kinship of bodies causes a magnet to attract a magnet or iron: so also it is not incredible concerning the Moon that it is moved by the kindred body of the Earth, although no contact of the bodies intervenes in either case. And so 7th, what wonder is it that the Moon is moved by the Earth, when we see in turn that the Moon, by its passage over the zenith of places, causes the reciprocal ebb and flow of the Ocean on the Earth? Is this not a sufficiently evident proof of the communication of motions between these two bodies? Finally, 8th, the same is confirmed by this remaining part of the analogy: the Sun and the Earth rotate around their own axes (which is certain by experience regarding the Sun itself, and regarding the Earth at least according to Copernicus), namely so that by this rotation they may impart motion to the planets positioned around them—the Sun to the six primaries, the Earth to the Moon. Therefore, this species <note>Johannes Kepler uses the term "species" to describe a physical force or emanation that radiates from a celestial body to move another</note>, which is sixty times larger than the Earth, permeates—I say—the entire orbit of the Moon thirty times in a single month, whereas the Moon returns to the same point only once within that same span of time, having followed the species of the Earth. It has just been stated that at both times <note>referring to the New and Full Moon</note> the motion is equal.

      *From where, then, does that additional disparity of effect come, so that it greatly accelerates the motion of the Moon in the D. H. Conjunctions <note>original: "Copulis," referring to the New and Full Moon where the Sun, Earth, and Moon align</note>, but does nothing in the F. K. Quadratures <note>The quarter-moons, where the Moon is at a 90-degree angle from the Sun</note>? And what, on the contrary, retards the motion of the Moon in the F. K. Quadratures?*

   No part of celestial physics has been more difficult to explain than this: in order to resolve it as far as possible, we must use the diagram on page 560.

   You will remember, therefore, that all the circles which bound the illumination of the Moon's globe, such as CD, GH, and the rest, are parts of just as many spherical surfaces into which the light coming from the Sun as a center is spread out; but the circle DFHK represents the species <term>species: a philosophical term for the "image" or "influence" emanating from a body</term> of the body of the Earth AB, situated in its center, which moves the Moon. You see that in the D. H. Conjunctions, the species of light CD and the species of the Earth's body OCDL are applied to each other by contact, which in L. M. N. O. intersect each other at oblique angles, so that the application is more imperfect; but in the EF, IK Quadratures, the intersection occurs at right angles: therefore, the application is clearly non-existent, since the intersection of the Moon tends toward the center of the Earth, and a mere point of the circle NIO corresponds to it.

   Since, therefore, no other cause for the acceleration in the Conjunctions appears, it must be established that a strengthening faculty for the Earth's moving species ODL exists in the light CD separately—not now insofar as its source (that is, the body of the Sun) rotates (this modification from motion was valid above, when we were speaking of the species of the bodies of the Sun and Earth themselves without respect to light), but insofar as it is light; namely, according to the genuine and, in a certain way, essential configuration of light. If, therefore, we establish that this species of the Earth's body is strengthened by the modes of its application to the spheres of light, the cause and measure of the very strong acceleration in the CD and GH Conjunctions, and none at all in the Quadratures, will be at hand.

The force of light contributes to the stimulation of the Moon <note>The author uses "incitandam" to describe the acceleration or driving force acting upon the lunar body</note> even in the preceding direction <term>MHN</term> <note>referring to a specific arc or segment in the author's geometric diagram</note>, with respect to the center of the Sun; specifically at that time when the Moon appears to us empty of light, or joined with the Sun <note>The New Moon phase, or conjunction</note>. Therefore, light does not provide the direction to the motion by itself, but rather through the stimulated species <term>MHN</term> <note>The "species" here refers to the Aristotelian or Keplerian concept of a physical emanation or "image" of force transmitted through space</note>.

->*If this force is inherent in light, a greater force will be present in the denser light around GH, namely in the vicinity of the Sun; a lesser force in the more scattered light around the full Moon in CD, when it is a thirtieth part of the distance further from the Sun: will the New Moon therefore be faster than the Full Moon, all other things being equal?*<-

The more perfect application of the light compensates for the weakness of the light at <term>CD</term> <note>the Full Moon position</note>, because the cavity of <term>CD</term> is flatter than at <term>GH</term> <note>the New Moon position</note>. Since, therefore, the strengthening occurs through the application of the "species": in the Full Moon, the more scattered light, being applied more perfectly, performs just as much as the denser light does in the "silent" Moon <note>original: "silente"; a classical term for the New Moon when it is not visible</note> when applied less perfectly. Furthermore, the distances between the Moon and the Sun are the same as those which measure out the density of the light and the respective curvatures of the circles <term>CD</term> and <term>GH</term>; for this reason, the compensation is made perfect.

**BOOK FOUR. 565**

The Moon is accelerated by 1 minute and 26 seconds in one degree at the syzygies <note>original: "copulis"; the points where the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned, i.e., New and Full Moon</note>, and is retarded by the same amount in one degree at the quadratures <note>the points where the Moon is at a 90-degree angle from the Sun</note>. Therefore, if the retardation is canceled out by a double acceleration, the maximum acceleration at the syzygies will be 2 minutes and 52 seconds. Thus, if the squared sines of all 90 degrees contribute their small portions into one sum, we will accumulate 2 degrees and 9 minutes; therefore, in a sidereal year, this equals 106 degrees and 22 minutes, rather than the 132 degrees and 45 minutes required.

But first, the quantity of the maximum "Variation" <note>a specific inequality in the Moon's motion discovered by Tycho Brahe</note> is not entirely certain in Tycho's work, who shows it as 40 and a half minutes at the 45th degree. Thus, if it is set at 51 minutes, we equal the prescribed sum. By taking the acceleration of the first degree as 3 minutes, 34 seconds, and 40 thirds (or Tycho’s form of 1 minute, 47 seconds, and 20 thirds, with an equal retardation at the ninetieth degree, or in the Quadratures), a sum of 2 degrees and 41 minutes is collected in one quadrant. This value will acquire great probability later when we discuss the causes of inequalities. Furthermore, even if we strictly retain Tycho’s small quantity at the 45th degree, the preceding and following values could be distributed in a form other than Tycho’s to produce the desired sum; or perhaps minute causes remain hidden from us which subtract something from those 133 degrees in the treatment of the Variation.

*By what proportion, then, do you think the*
*monthly motion of the Moon around the Earth is distributed*
*between these two causes: namely, the species of the*
*body of the Earth, and the circle of*
*illumination of the bodies?*

We see that while the Earth revolves around its own axis thirty times (minus less than a half), the Moon meanwhile returns once around the Earth—that is, from Sun to Sun. Thus it happens that in one year, or 365 days, 6 hours, 9 minutes, and 26 seconds, the Moon returns twelve times, and adds more than a third of a thirteenth revolution—that is, 132 degrees and three-quarters. It is therefore agreeable that the density of the matter in the body of the Moon is so tempered to that degree...

# BOOK FOUR. 569

The archetypal <note>The "archetypal" refers to the original divine blueprint or geometric model of the universe</note> [creator] cuts off a measure of contraction from the Zodiac, from which are owed proportionally to the length of the Lunar year 5 degrees, 6 minutes, and 41 seconds. Therefore, the Moon is raised by just as many degrees, so that even if these are not completed in the mundane space <note>The physical space of the world as opposed to the abstract geometric model</note>, it nevertheless returns to the Sun for the twelfth time. These degrees are worth 10 hours and 4 minutes; when these are subtracted from the discovered 19 hours and 33 minutes, there remain as an appendix to the 354 days, 9 hours and 29 minutes. For this value, the astronomical tables provide 8 hours and 49 minutes, which is only two-thirds of an hour less. This small difference can be attributed to other minute circumstances. In the meantime, it has been proven accurately enough by both methods that this aberration of numbers from whole and beautiful integers arises from the concurrence of the causes of the Moon's motion. The reason is now clear why 360 is almost the mean proportional between the lengths of the Lunar year and the Sidereal Solar year.

## BOOK IV
## PART III.

### Concerning the real and true inequality of the motions of the Planets, and its causes.

#### From where do the Planets get their name, which in Latin sounds like "Wanderers"? <note>The word "Planet" is derived from the Greek 'planētēs', meaning wanderer</note>

From that manifold variety of their own motions, which, if you follow the judgment of the eyes, has no law, no certain circle, and no defined time when compared with the fixed stars.

#### In how many ways do the Planets appear to wander?

In three ways. 1. In the longitude of the sphere of fixed stars, which we said extends along the Ecliptic <note>The apparent path of the Sun across the celestial sphere</note>. 2. In width <note>Latitude, or the distance north or south of the ecliptic</note>,

<note>original: "Epitomes Astronomiæ"</note>

either to the two sides of the Ecliptic <note>The apparent path of the Sun across the sky</note>, toward its poles.
3. In depth, that is, in a straight line extending from the center of vision into the depths of the ether. Although this variation is not detected by the eyes alone, reasoning is added based on the varied apparent size, both of the bodies themselves and of their orbital arcs.

      *What should be held regarding these errors of the*
            *planets: do they truly wander with all that*
                  *variety, or is it only the*
                        *sight that is deceived?*

      Although that motion is not present in the bodies of the planets exactly as it strikes the eyes—for many deceptions of sight creep in here—nevertheless, once these deceptions have been mentally removed, there still remains some inequality of motions, and it exists in reality in all the planets.

            *What then is that true motion of the planets*
                  *through their*
                        *circumstances?*

      It is indeed constant, as far as complete periods <note>The time taken to complete one full orbit</note> are concerned; and it moves around the Sun, the center of the world, perpetually following the sequence of the signs <note>Moving forward through the Zodiac</note>. It never clings to one place, appearing stationary, and much less does it ever become retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward</note>. But nevertheless, it is of unequal speed through its parts; it causes the planet in one certain part of the circuit to run further away from the Sun, and in the opposite part to come very close to the Sun. Where it runs further away, it is slower; where it approaches closer, it is faster. Finally, in one part of the circle it departs to the north from the Ecliptic, and in the other to the South. Therefore, a triple real inequality still remains for it: in length, in width, and in depth. This is what astronomers prove with suitable evidence, concerning which see Book VI.

2. Finally, Astronomy also bears witness to this, when treated with appropriate precision: that the individual paths or circuits of the planets are not arranged precisely into a perfect circle, but are made to be elliptical.

   Chiefly by four. 1. From the nature of the moving bodies. 2. From the nature of the moving power <note>The "moving power" or *virtus motrix* refers to the force Kepler believed emanated from the sun to move the planets.</note>. 3. From the nature of the place in which that motion occurs. 4. From the perfection of the circle.

->*State their argument from the nature*<-
->*of the bodies?*<-

   They reasoned thus: that those bodies are not composed of the elements <note>The four terrestrial elements: earth, air, fire, and water.</note>; therefore, neither generation nor corruption, nor any alteration, has any jurisdiction over them. They claimed the experience of all ages bears witness to this: for the same bodies are always observed, and nothing is found to be changed in their mass, their number, or their appearance. Now, however, the motions of elementary bodies are various and inconstant for this very reason: because the elements are variously mixed for their constitution, and they fight amongst themselves within those mixtures. Therefore, in the celestial realms, where there is no such mixing and no battle of elements within a mixture, there is also no place for turbulence and no place for inequality.

->*What do you think should be answered to this*<-

   If the argument speaks of a disordered turbulence of motions, there is indeed no such thing in heaven: there are no celestial tumults, such as occur in thunderclaps,
   *The flame and the dripping water fighting amongst themselves:* <note>original: "Pugnantum inter se flamma & stillantis aquæ"</note>
because the composition of the bodies of the world is of a very different kind. But if the argument also excludes every regular inequality

<margin><unclear>illegible</unclear></margin> is opposed to [uniformity]; now, certainly not every instance of this regular intensification and relaxation of motions arises from the battle and mixture of elements within the moved bodies, nor from the fact that they are changeable. For a certain inequality of motions arises from this very fact: that they are bodies—both those that are moved and those that apply the motion—and because they consist of their own matter, their own quantity, and their own shape, both internally and externally. According to these quantities and shapes, they are also endowed with their own natural power <term>potentia naturali: the inherent capacity of an object to act or be acted upon</term>, which has less effect on a distant movable object than on a nearby one; in this case, the faculties of the mover and the moved yield to one another rather than fight. 574 EPITOME OF ASTRONOMY

Therefore, there is no reason why they should move their spheres differently at different times. And so, because of this very nature of the minds <note>referring to the "moving intelligences" or spirits that ancient and medieval philosophers believed guided the planets</note>, the shapes of the motions must be the most perfect circles.

*What do you oppose to this?*

Even if the motive power is neither a God nor a mind, one must still concede what the argument intends, partly even regarding that motive cause which a truer philosophy suggests—namely, the natural power of bodies. Wherever and insofar as such a power acts alone, it moves most uniformly and in a perfect circle, and it does so by the sole necessity of its effort and the perennial simplicity of its essence. This occurs in the rotation of the bodies of the Sun (and perhaps also the Earth), which arises from a single motive cause, whether that be a quality of the body or an offspring of the soul <note>Kepler often used "soul" (anima) to describe the internal force or "motive faculty" that causes a celestial body to rotate on its axis</note> innate to the body. For the axis remains with its two opposite poles, while the body revolves around the axis most uniformly and most circularly. This would also happen if any planetary globe remained at the same distance from the Sun; for it would be swept by the Sun into a most perfect circle most uniformly, by means of the emitted immaterial species <note>term: immaterial species; Kepler's concept of a force-field, like magnetism, that transmits influence through space without physical matter</note> of the solar body, which is established in a most uniform motion of gyration. By this same most uniform motion, that species of the body also goes around in the breadth of the mundane space, like a stirred-up vortex.

But although we have so far conceded the argument of the ancients, it does not yet follow from this that there is an all-encompassing uniformity of motions. For there concur in the motion not only the motive power and the mobile body, but also the internal rectilinear configuration of the mobile body. Depending on its different position relative to the Sun, this body is affected differently in its motion: from one side it is repelled, and from the other it is drawn inward. There also concurs the rest of the magnetic axis of the mobile body in a parallel position; from this internal rest, and from the carrying-around that comes from the outside, there arises that change of position.

<summary>Kepler argues that while a single force acting alone would produce a perfect circle, planetary orbits are complex because they result from the interaction between the Sun's rotating force and the planet's own magnetic properties.</summary>
<keywords>motive power, celestial physics, solar rotation, immaterial species, magnetic axis, planetary motion, circularity vs. complexity</keywords>

Thus, in respect to the meeting of so many requirements, the force moving the planet cannot be called "simple," because it moves the planet at different degrees of its own species.

*What was the argument of the ancients based on*
*location?*

They gathered their reasoning thus: that the Elemental region is around the center of the world, and the Heaven is at the surface. Therefore, to elemental bodies belongs straight motion, which has a beginning and an end, and which—distributed by the contrary principles of gravity and levity <note>heaviness and lightness</note>—brings each of those bodies back into its own place. From this it follows that according to the varying approach to the natural place (as if to a target), there is also a varying speed, and finally, pure rest. But celestial bodies are engaged perpetually in the circular space of the world: which serves as an argument that they are neither heavy nor light. Nor are they moved for the sake of rest or for occupying a place (since they are always in their place), but are moved only so that they may be moved. Therefore, it was argued that their motion must be uniform, and the type of motion must be something other than rectilinear—namely, a type suited to the eternity of motion, which is to say, returning into itself.

*What do you answer to this third*
*argument?*

Not every inequality of motions arises from gravity and levity, which are properties of the elements; but some also arise from a change in distance, as is evident in the lever and the balance scale. And this cause produces the intensification of celestial motions...

Meanwhile, one must be careful to note that there is nonetheless some relationship between the principles of gravity and levity in the elements, and the natural inertia <term>inertia: the inherent resistance of matter to motion</term> of a planetary globe toward movement; however, this relationship does not account for any inequality of motion.

As for what concerns the shape of the motion, the argument concludes no more than what we ourselves can grant: namely, that the motion is reflected back into itself, a quality held not only by circular motion, but also by elliptical motion. Therefore, the premises are not denied. For truly, bodies that revolve around their own axes move only to this extent: that by their perennial motion they serve some necessity of their own globe, and some even move so that they may carry the planets around themselves in perennial circuits.

*State the fourth argument of the ancients, derived from the circular figure?*

They philosophized in this way: that of all motions returning into themselves, the circular is the simplest and most perfect; and that in all others, such as the oval and similar shapes, there is some mixture of straightness. Therefore, they argued this circular motion is most suited to the simplest nature of bodies, to the divine moving minds <note>original: "divinis mentib. motricibus" — referring to the Aristotelian idea of Intelligences that move the spheres</note> (since its beauty and perfection are something mental), and finally to the heavens, which possess a spherical figure.

*How is this to be refuted?*

To these points I respond thus: first, if the celestial motions were the work of a Mind, as those ancients believed, it would be quite plausibly concluded that the paths of the planets are perfectly circular. For then the form of motion conceived by the Mind would serve as a rule and goal for the power to which the motion is directed. But celestial motions are not the work of a Mind, but of Nature—that is, the natural power of bodies, or of a Soul acting according to those bodily powers...

<summary>Kepler argues that while ancient philosophers insisted on circular orbits due to their perceived perfection, planetary motion is actually a physical result of natural forces and inertia, which allows for elliptical paths.</summary>

This bears witness to a natural, corporeal power, and to the emanation and quantities of its specific kind.

Next, even if we were to grant them <note>the traditionalist philosophers or Scholastics</note> the existence of "intelligences" <note>term: Intelligences; celestial spirits or angels believed by ancients to manually guide the planets</note>, they still do not obtain what they desire: namely, the absolute perfection of the circle. For if it were only a matter of the beauty of the circle, the circle would indeed be most rightly perceived by the mind, and it would decorate any bodies whatsoever—especially the celestial ones—since they participate in quantity, and the circle is the most beautiful quantity. But because, in addition to the mind, there would then also be a need for natural and animal faculties to effect the movement, those faculties would follow their own nature. They would not perform everything according to the dictate of a mind (which they would not perceive), but would perform many things out of material necessity. It is no wonder, therefore, if these faculties, when mixed together, were unable to achieve perfection entirely. The ancients themselves concede that the paths of the planets are eccentric <note>term: Eccentric; a circular orbit where the center is not the Earth</note>, which seems a much greater deformity than an elliptical path. And yet, through the providence of their "minds," they were unable to avoid this deformity.

However, I have often warned that while I deny that celestial motions are the work of a mind, I am not then speaking of the Creator Mind. To Him, indeed, all things are fitting, whether they be circular or elliptical, whether they are to be administered and represented through minds, or whether they are compelled by material necessity from principles once established.

## II. On the causes of inequality in longitude.

*What causes do you therefore provide for why—even though all the paths of the primary planets are arranged around the Sun—the angles (by which the different parts of a single planet's path are viewed, as if from the center of the Sun) are nonetheless not completed by the planet in proportional times?* <note>The "inequality in longitude" refers to the observation that planets do not appear to move at a constant speed across the sky when viewed from the Sun.</note>

Two causes concur, one optical and the other physical, each being of almost equal effect. The first cause is that the path of the planet is not drawn around the Sun at an equal distance on all sides, but one part of it is near to the Sun, while the opposite part is just as much farther away from the Sun. Now, of equal parts, those nearby are viewed at a larger angle, and those far away at a smaller angle; and of those viewed at an equal angle, the nearby ones are actually smaller, and the remote ones larger. <note>This is the "optical" cause: a perspective effect where objects appear to move slower when they are further away.</note> The second cause is that the planet is actually slower at a greater distance from the Sun, and faster at a shorter distance. <note>This is the "physical" cause, later known as Kepler's Second Law: planets physically speed up as they approach the Sun.</note>
Therefore, when these two causes are combined into one, it is easily apparent that of two arcs appearing equal to the sight, a greater time is required for the one that is inherently larger, but a much greater time still because of the real slowness of the planet in that more remote arc.

*Could not one cause alone suffice? For instance, since the planet's orbit altogether recedes further from the Sun on one side than on the opposite side, could we not make that distance so great that this entire apparent inequality might be explained by this unequal distance of the parts of the orbit alone?*

Observations do not allow us to make the inequality of the distances as great as the inequality

<summary>Johannes Kepler explains that the apparent change in a planet's speed is caused by two factors: the optical illusion of perspective and the physical reality that planets move slower when further from the Sun.</summary>

The quality of time in which a planet completes equal angles relative to the Sun; but these facts testify that the inequality of the intervals <note>The varying distances between the planet and the Sun</note> is sufficient to account for at least half of this inequality: the remainder, therefore, arises from the real acceleration and deceleration of the planet.

*What are the laws and examples of this speed and slowness?*

A true example is found in the balance scale: for just as in that case, when the arms are in equilibrium, the proportion of the weights suspended from each arm is the reciprocal of the proportion of the arms themselves. For a greater weight suspended from a shorter arm balances a smaller weight suspended from a longer arm. Thus, as the short arm relates to the long one, so the weight on the longer arm relates to the weight on the shorter one. And if we now mentally remove one arm, and in place of its weight we conceive an equal power in the fulcrum itself for lifting the remaining arm with its weight; then it appears that this power of the fulcrum is not as capable against a weight at a distance as it is against the same weight when it is near. This resistance snatches the planet, as if from the hands of the rotating Sun, so that the planet does not exactly follow that grasping force.

Another astronomical example was given above in the third book, when we said that the axis of the Earth's rotation remains perpetually in the same parallel position while the Earth is carried around the Sun. <note>See page 248 of the original edition.</note>

*What causes, therefore, do you provide for the direction of the magnetic fibers of a planetary body toward the same region of the world throughout the planet's entire circuit?*

The same causes that were indicated above in Book I, page 116, by which the axis of the Earth's rotation is fixed. For, in the first place, the parallel position of the fibers represents a certain identity, which is rest rather than motion. Therefore, the cause of that position does not seem to be some positive or active natural power, but rather a privative state <note>A "privative" state refers to the absence of a quality—in this case, the absence of motion.</note> of all motion. And so, that natural inertia of matter toward motion seems to have an internal rectilinear configuration; and being extended along these fibers, or rendered stronger and more insurmountable by the condensation of parts in a straight line.
If this is less likely: let there be, then, distinct <term>impotencies</term> <note>original: "ἀδυναμίαι" (adynamiai). Immediately, however, as the globe is carried past this point E of its orbit toward F—because the discordant hemisphere now becomes closer to the Sun than the friendly one and turns more and more toward the Sun—the planet also begins to be pushed away <note>original: "extrudi"</note> from the Sun, as if out of a narrower and denser sphere of the solar species into a wider, thinner, and weaker one. This happens again around G, the other quadrant of the circuit. As the planet is carried further toward H, this expulsion relaxes again until it vanishes entirely at A, with the planet restored to its original place and expelled to the farthest distance from the Sun.

But in the meantime, I would not rigidly deny that this effect was rather a matter of design; so that it is not, or is not merely, an appendix of necessity: because we are still ignorant of its quantity. Then there will be an occasion for stating the final cause <note>The "final cause" refers to the ultimate purpose or "why" behind a natural phenomenon</note>; that the tempering of the forces among themselves—of libration, of the inclination of the fibers, and of the revolution—tends toward this in a certain proportion in each one: so that because the librations were indeed arranged to establish the Harmonies of the motions, any one of the Harmonies would come forth not always in one single configuration of two planets, but through the passage of centuries would wander through absolutely all configurations: and thus all the Harmonies of motions (which are the subject of Book V of the *Harmonics*) would be mingled with all the Harmonies of configurations (the material of Book IV of the *Harmonics*).

## IV. On the Motion in Latitude.

*By what laws do the Planets deviate to the*
*sides of the Ecliptic?* <note>The Ecliptic is the apparent path of the Sun against the stars; "latitude" here refers to how far a planet moves north or south of that path.</note>

Again, by a most simple law: namely, that the plane which they circumscribe with the center of their body is, in any given period, exactly straight and inclined toward the plane of the Ecliptic with a constant and invariable inclination; except in the case of the Moon.

*If uniform planes are inclined toward one*
*another, they meet and intersect each other in a*
*single straight line: I ask, what is that common*
*line upon which the planet's orbit is inclined*
*toward the Ecliptic?*

In all planets, that line passes through the center of the Sun; and the line of each planet is extended into its own specific places in the Ecliptic, which are opposite to one another from the center of the Sun.

*From what evidence is this established?*

It is established from the fact that when a Planet, in two different parts of its revolution—as in the following diagram at C and D—is seen upon the Ecliptic, lacking any latitude, these two locations are found through calculation to be in the same straight line CAD with the Sun at A. For example, if ACM were to fall in 17 degrees of Taurus, the interval of time until the planet was again seen on the Ecliptic, combined with the hypothesis of the Eccentric <note>The "Eccentric" refers to the circular path of a planet where the center of the circle is offset from the Sun.</note>, shows the line ADO of the other location of the Eccentric to be in 17 degrees of Scorpio: that is, in the opposite position to 17 degrees of Taurus.

*What is gathered from this?*

The very same thing as above, on page 540. For since the planes of all six Eccentrics meet in one common center, the Sun: therefore, except in this center of the Sun, they can nowhere all meet at once, because the line of intersection is not common to all, but to each—

Therefore, because the Sun is the common node <note>The "node" here refers to the central intersection point of all planetary paths.</note> of all systems: it follows that whether nature moves the planets by physical forces, or a Mind moves them by rational commands; the Sun is entirely the target for the planets, toward which all revolutions look.

*What causes do you provide for the motion in latitude?* <note>In astronomy, "latitude" refers to the north or south deviation of a planet from the Ecliptic, the apparent path of the Sun.</note>

The Sun is not the cause of this deviation from the plane of the Ecliptic, except in a remote sense; nor do the planets require a Mind for this task, nor the previously refuted construction of solid spheres <note>Kepler refers to the ancient Greek idea that planets were carried on physical, crystalline spheres, which he famously proved did not exist.</note> in which they might be carried along a proper orbit as if in chariots. This is even less necessary for this motion than it is for the oscillations in height and depth, or for the motion in longitude: rather, some specific formation of the planetary bodies themselves is sufficient alone to twist their orbits away from and back toward the Ecliptic.

*Why is the Sun not the cause, since it has already been stated that the lines of the sections pass through the body of the Sun itself?*

Because one and the same Sun, with one and the same form of its body—which circulates in a uniform and most direct stream beneath the circle midway between the poles of the Sun's rotation—cannot seize different planets through various other paths, unless the planets themselves add causes for this diverse departure to the sides from their own nature.

*What kind of formation of the planetary bodies do you suggest?*

It can be either essential, namely internal rectilinear magnetic fibers; or accidental, specifically the revolution of the planetary globe around its own axis, arranged in such a way that the fibers or the axis of rotation retain a parallel position throughout the entire circuit of the body; and it is directed so that when the planet is beneath the Ecliptic <note>The apparent path of the Sun across the sky</note>, it touches the orbit and deflects with one end somewhat toward the Northern region and with the other toward the South.

*Do you have a common example of this deflection?*

The oars of ships provide an example of sorts. For if a ship is driven forward by the winds, but the oar is tied obliquely to the stern: then the ship is gradually pushed to the side, contrary to the direction the line of the wind carries it.

*An oar, a pole, or a rudder always directs a ship in only one direction; how then do the planets now move out to the sides of the Ecliptic, and then return from there to the Ecliptic?*

If the oar of the ship is turned, the ship also deflects to the other side. Although the planets hold their fibers straight, in a parallel position and unturned, they are nevertheless transported to the opposite parts of their circuit, in which the fibers—

But since this motion of the Moon around the Earth, as explained above, is derived from two sources, as it were—namely, from the daily rotation of the Earth, which is the center of the Moon's small heaven, and from the rotation of the Sun around its own axis (the Sun being the center of the Great Orb common to both the Earth and the Moon's heaven)—it is indeed reasonable that the true and real motion of the Moon around the Earth should have two sources. This remains true even when the mind sets aside that common circulation around the Sun, which is accidental to the entire heaven of the Moon. It should undergo all those double affections which the motions of the primary planets <note>The planets orbiting the Sun directly, such as Mars or Jupiter</note> possess individually. And this accords excellently with experience, the decrees of the experts, and the very terms arising from this duplication. For not only in the previous sections—where there was a solitary mean motion <note>The average speed of a planet</note> in one of the primary planets—was there both a mean motion and a semi-monthly variation of this mean in the Moon; but also in this place, when dealing with the periodic inequality of this motion (which is not semi-monthly like the variation, but monthly, or rather semi-annual), we detect a double intensification and slowing of the Moon's mean motion at opposite moments of the period, instead of the simple version found in a primary planet. Finally, instead of the simple lateral digression of the primary planets, we find a double one here as well.

### What is the cause of the quantity of the Moon's Eccentricity?

In my *Harmonics* <note>referring to his work *Harmonices Mundi*</note>, I demonstrate that the variety of the Moon's motions determines precisely a *diatessaron* <note>A musical interval of a perfect fourth</note>; this seems to have an affinity with the Quadratures <note>The quarter-moon phases</note> and Conjunctions of the Moon. Therefore, so that this interval could be represented by a composite motion, the Eccentricity was made to be of such a size.

*What distinction is perceived between*
*those common inequalities of the Moon with the planets, and*

1. Just as there were two elements, as it were, of the Moon's motion around the Earth in the preceding sections—one arising from the Earth rotating around its axis, the other from the application of Solar light to this moving species of the Earth—of which the former was free from the Moon's phases and the latter bound to the phases: so now also of the two inequalities, the first indeed, an accident <note>In the Aristotelian sense: a property or quality</note> of the first element or mean motion, is found to have its own proper limits, which we shall call the Apogee of the Moon <note>The point in the orbit farthest from Earth</note>: the first form of digression to the sides <note>Latitude</note> also has its own limits, distinct from the limits of the Apogee, which they call the Limits and Nodes. But the latter inequality, an accident of the second element or "copular incitation" <note>The additional force Kepler attributes to the sun's light acting on the moon</note>, called by Ptolemy the "Annulus of the Epicycle," has limits in common with the lunar month and the phases; as does the second form of digression to the sides.

2. That former inequality, of both longitude and latitude, is always constant through all periods, namely of perpetually the same quantity: of the latter ones, each becomes greatest in only one month of each semester, smaller in the rest, and in some, which divide the year into two parts, almost nothing; namely where the opposite affections of this second acceleration and retardation, likewise of Northern and Southern latitude, begin to migrate into contrary halves of the Lunations.

3. Therefore, those former inequalities have both their quantity and their laws of distribution from their own proper causes: but the second ones receive their quantities and affections from the presence of the first ones in any one semicircle of a lunation; they have only the laws of distribution separate, and accommodated to the circuits of the lunations, yet similar to the former ones.

4.       *Is this second inequality of longitude therefore truly caused by some second Eccentricity, or a departure of the Moon from the Earth, just as the first inequality has its cause in the change of distance?*

      No: the observation of the Moon's parallaxes <note>Parallax is the apparent shift in position of a celestial body when viewed from different points on Earth; Kepler uses it here to measure distance.</note>, combined with the study of Eclipses, refutes this; and the reasons concerning the proportion of the bodies, proposed *a priori* <note>From first principles or theoretical reasoning.</note> in the first part of this fourth book, are in agreement. But this also can be argued: that absolutely no change in distance occurs tied to the phases <note>The "phases" refer to the Moon's position relative to the Sun (New Moon, Full Moon, etc.).</note>; because, while various craftsmen correct one another regarding this hypothesis, the quantity of this change has been made smaller and smaller. Ptolemy established an enormous change; which Regiomontanus <note>Johannes Müller von Königsberg (1436–1476), a key Renaissance astronomer.</note> refuted; Copernicus halved it, and transposed it from the form of an Eccentric into the form of a second Epicycle <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one.</note>: Tycho Brahe in turn corrected this, claiming a portion for the "equating circle," which he himself, along with Copernicus, was accustomed to justify through an Epicycle of doubled motion. I have exchanged the Conjunctional intervals with the Quadratures <note>The "Quadratures" are the points where the Moon is 90 degrees from the Sun.</note>, and transposed the circuits from a month into a year: but in later times, leaning upon these discoveries, I finally detected that absolutely no change in distance occurs through the cycles of the phases.

      *From where, then, does that second acceleration and retardation, tied to the phases, arise?*

      From the varying relationship of the Moon's eccentric orbit to the phases. For while it goes around the Earth (its mover) by a simple and perpetually uniform law of Eccentricity—in the same way that any of the primary planets goes around the Sun—it happens by accident that it is distant in different ways at different times from the other promoter of its motion, which accelerates it in the Conjunctions <note>The "Conjunctions" (Copulae) refer to the New and Full Moon positions.</note>. For if its longer distance from the Earth falls during the Conjunctions, where the acceleration is greatest, then the species <note>Kepler uses "species" to refer to the moving force or "image" emanating from a body.</note> of the Earth, spread out in a more diffused circle,

-> What if the longer distance is directed toward the Sun? Will the motion also be weakened in that case? And yet, the Moon then runs its course in denser light. <-

Undoubtedly, this is what we cautioned against above. For the light of the Sun does not move things by itself, but through the "species" <note>an emanation or physical influence</note> of the body of the Earth, to which it transmits the laws and modes of its work. Therefore, just as the light did not provide the direction of motion above, but rather the species of the Earth's body did—sometimes in a direction plainly contrary to the direction in which the Sun moves around its own axis—so now also the motive species from the Earth is strengthened according to the proportion of its native strength: weakly where it is weak (namely, at a longer distance from the Earth as its source), and strongly where it is strong (at a shorter distance from the Earth), regardless of the variation in the Moon's distance from the Sun.

It now seems possible to hold no other view than this very respect for equality, as the simplest and therefore the most beautiful proportion.
      Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian astronomer</note>, however, presents a slightly larger measure, and exactly as much as we previously gathered from the appendix—13 degrees, 45 minutes for 12 conjunctions—as the Variation of one quadrant: namely, 2 degrees, 41 minutes. But if this measure and quantity is to be maintained on both sides, then the cause seems to be transferred from a deliberate design to a geometric necessity: namely, that the increase of the interval (that is, the Eccentricity <term>Eccentricity: the deviation of an orbit from a perfect circle</term>) completely exhausts what the stimulation from light had provided in that conjunction; conversely, in the other conjunction, the Eccentricity subtracted from the interval adds as much to the speed as that stimulation of light also produced.
      Thus, in a month that lacks the synodic equation <note>The "synodic equation" refers to the correction needed for the Moon's position relative to the Sun</note>—as when in this Diagram the Apogee <term>Apogee: the point in the orbit farthest from the Earth</term> is in EF and the perigee in IK—the parts of the light-based stimulation in each conjunction are equal, because the distances between the Moon and the Earth in each conjunction, such as AC and AH, are equal in that month. In the succeeding months, as an inequality of intervals gradually arises in the conjunctions (for instance, if L were the Apogee and N the perigee, then certainly distance AC would be greater than AH), there also arises some monthly equation, which is always greatest in EF and IK during that entire month. Finally, in that month in which there is a full synodic equation (as if the Apogee were in CD), the stimulation in the CD conjunction is zero, while in the other, GH, it is double the stimulation in the previously mentioned month. Then in the F and K quadrants, the equation is the greatest of all that can occur in the whole year. But in G, nearest the perigee, the tiny parts of the equation become fourfold: 1. Optical, as in the planets. 2. Physical, as in the planets. 3. Variation from light. 4. The intensification of the same due to the diminished interval. The proportion of these parts among themselves is a matter of geometric necessity; but the sum fused from all four is so tempered by design that this perigee motion of the Moon at GH in conjunction, compared to the apogee motion of the Moon at CD in the quadrant, would be as 4 to 3, and would be the Harmony of the Fourth <note>original: "Harmonia Diateſſaron." Kepler frequently linked planetary motions to musical intervals.</note>.

# EPITOME OF ASTRONOMY 618

But as for the true cause why these two things—which are bound together by no necessity—should behave as they do: namely, 1. the manner of the <term>copular acceleration</term><note>The "copula" refers to the syzygies, or the alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon at new and full moon.</note>, and 2. the manner of the eccentricity; and yet the eccentricity precisely cancels out the acceleration in the apogean <insert>far point</insert> alignment, and doubles it in the perigean <insert>near point</insert> alignment: this, I say, I have not yet been able to investigate.

*What probable cause do you provide for such great speed of the <term>Apsides</term><note>The points in an orbit closest to or farthest from the center, such as the perigee and apogee.</note> and the limits of the Moon, if the Apsides and limits of the primary planets are incomparably slower?*

Doubtless, here too the effect of the composition of the Moon's motive powers is rendered conspicuous. For just as we said above that the simple force of the Earth was tempered to <term>Harmonic numbers</term><note>Kepler believed the universe was designed according to musical and geometric harmonies.</note>—specifically, in revolving the body of the Earth around its axis to exactly 360 days, and in driving the Moon around the Earth to precisely 12 months in one year (or one revolution of the Earth's center around the Sun)—so now let us also say that in the inclination and restoration of the Moon's <term>fibers</term><note>Kepler's theory that planets contain magnetic "fibers" that interact with the Sun to govern their motion.</note>, by which the <term>libration</term><note>A slow rocking motion or oscillation.</note> and the deflections of latitude are performed, those simple forces are tempered to the length of the Moon's periodic time by the same proportion observed in the other planets. 

But just as above, because of the addition of help from the Sun—both for spinning the globe of the Earth like a top and for driving the Moon around—the <term>Archetypal numbers</term><note>The ideal mathematical ratios intended by the Creator.</note> were disturbed in the final effect; so that instead of 360 days, there were 365 and a quarter, and instead of 12 lunations in a year, there were about 12 and a third? So now also, because of this same increase in the Moon's acceleration from the Solar illumination, it happens that the Moon reaches the middle sides of its circuit before the fibers have been inclined by the proper measure. Therefore, at a deeper place than the fourth part from the Apside, the fiber looks toward the Sun; and when this happens, we have emphasized above that a transposition of the Apsides occurs. It is reasonable that this transposition of the Apsides should be quite sensible <insert>noticeable</insert>, because that increase <margin>increase</margin> is sensible.

Philosophers ought to strive all the more because the Moon—besides so many other proofs—is also our teacher in this specific inquiry for acquiring knowledge of the celestial bodies, and she shines ahead by her own example, illuminating the nature of all the planets.

->*By what reasoning does it happen that the Moon, besides its usual periodic latitudes, also makes synodic <term>synodic: the time between successive conjunctions with the Sun, like from new moon to new moon</term> excursions to the North and South?*<-

That force of light, strengthening the species <note>original: "speciem"; here referring to the "immaterial image" or "emanation" of the Earth that Kepler believed moved the Moon</note> of the Earth which moves the Moon, just as it borrows the direction of motion and the proportions of its work from the very thing it strengthens; and just as it also passes into the character of the orbit itself for the sake of longitude <note>referring to the forward motion along the ecliptic</note>, according to the measure of their mutual application; so it must be established that it does the same for the sake of latitude. It facilitated the motion in length because it is itself extended in length: therefore, it will also facilitate the motion in breadth, because it also possesses the other extension of latitude—that is, because light is a surface, participating in density, as we have often cited from the study of optics. In the conjunctions <note>original: "copulis"; referring to the alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon</note> there-

*Since you attribute everything to the physical fibers of the globes, and to the immaterial species <note>The "species" refers to the radiating influence or "image" of a body's power, a common term in 17th-century physics</note> of the rotating bodies of the Sun and the Earth, and finally to the light of the Sun and the strengthening cause, do you leave nothing for the animal faculties? You seem to philosophize just as if someone were to contend that the triple fibers of the stomach were sufficient for its duties, and that there was no need for an animal faculty <note>The "animal faculty" refers to the soul's power to govern biological functions</note>?*

On the contrary, I admit a Soul in the body of the Sun, which is set in charge of the Sun's rotation and is the dispenser of the entire motion of the World: nor did I simply deny in Book I that there are individual souls even for the bodies of the planets, set in charge of the rotation of those bodies. But just as it is not necessary to introduce a specific soul into the fibers of the stomach—for it is sufficient that one common soul from the heart or liver, through its own species or through heat, flows out into the stomach and uses the faculties of its fibers—so also in the world it seems sufficient that this species (as of light, as of heat, so also, if you please) of the Solar soul, sent out together with light and heat, penetrates even to those places from which light and heat are excluded, namely: into the internal fibers of the bodies. Thus, just as the soul in the body can do nothing without the organ of the stomach, so also this soul of the world can do nothing without these laws and the Geometric arrangement of the bodies.

Let the status of the controversy therefore be observed: for it is one thing to simply refer every method of dispensing celestial motion—even if it involves contradictions and is therefore impossible—to the occult powers of some soul, while rejecting the physical instruments and all the modes which the human mind can devise; which is

622 EPITOMES OF ASTRONOMY

is the refuge <note>original: "κρησφύγετον" (kresphygeton), a Greek term for a place of safety or a loophole</note> of all ignorance and the very death of all philosophy. Yet, it is most commonly used by many who write or speak on astronomical matters, and was even noted above in Ptolemy himself. Another approach is first to examine everything within the bodies themselves that is adapted for motion, so that the possibility of these movements becomes apparent, even through popular examples. Only then, finally, should one pour over all these parts—just as one would a human body joined together by all its muscles and nerves—a motivating Soul. If this Soul can carry out any duties using bodily instruments, it will have no need for deliberation or discourse, which are the proper works of an intelligent soul. Conversely, if it performed everything through deliberation and discourse, it would have no need for those bodily instruments.

In short, the philosophers have devised "intelligences" <note>Kepler refers to the medieval scholastic idea that angels or divine minds moved the planets</note> which derive the motions of the heavens from themselves, as if from a guidebook, and which employ consensus, will, love, self-understanding, and finally, command. To me, these souls—or motivating forces—are of a lower kind; they provide only the impetus (as if it were the "matter" of the motion) through a uniform exertion of strength without the help of a mind. However, they find the laws (or the "form") of the motions within the bodies themselves. These bodies were indeed shaped by a Mind—not their own, but the Creator's—at the very beginning of the world, and were tempered to produce such motions.
